library(nlmixr2lib)

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Vu_2017_erenumab"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Vu_2017_erenumab"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1007/s11095-017-2183-6> (open access, PMC5533838)

Erenumab (AMG 334) is a fully human IgG2 monoclonal antibody against the
calcitonin gene-related peptide (CGRP) receptor. Binding to the receptor is
also a route of elimination, so its pharmacokinetics are nonlinear at low
concentrations. Vu 2017 pooled the phase 1 single- and multiple-ascending-dose
studies and fitted:

1. a **two-compartment quasi-steady-state (QSS) TMDD model** with first-order
   SC absorption, linear clearance, internalization of the drug-receptor
   complex, and a time-varying total receptor pool (Eqs. 1-4); and
2. a **direct sigmoid inhibitory model** of the capsaicin-induced increase in
   dermal blood flow (CIDBF), driven by the serum erenumab concentration
   (Eq. 7).

The CIDBF response is the difference between laser-Doppler dermal blood flow
30 min after and immediately before topical capsaicin, in perfusion units (PU).
Erenumab does not change blood flow before the capsaicin challenge.

# Population

108 subjects (60 SAD, 48 MAD; Tables I-II) at a single centre in Leuven,
Belgium: 80 healthy subjects and 28 migraine patients, 78% male, mean (SD) age
29.5 (9.7) years and weight 74.9 (11.9) kg (range 49-104 kg). The SAD study
gave SC 1, 7, 21, 70, 140 or 210 mg or IV 140 mg to healthy subjects and SC
140 mg to migraine patients; the MAD study gave SC 21, 70 or 140 mg Q4W x 3 or
280 mg then 210 mg x 2 Q4W to healthy subjects and SC 21 or 140 mg Q4W x 3 to
migraine patients. 1297 concentrations from 78 subjects and 676 dermal blood
flow measurements from 100 subjects (30 on placebo) were analysed.

The same information is available programmatically via
`readModelDb("Vu_2017_erenumab")()$population`.

# Source trace

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|----------------------|-------|-----------------|
| `lcl` (CL at 70 kg) | 0.214 L/day | Table III |
| `lvc` (Vc at 70 kg) | 4.27 L | Table III |
| `lq` (Q) | 3.34 L/day | Table III |
| `lvp` (Vp) | 2.73 L | Table III |
| `lka` (ka) | 0.432 1/day | Table III |
| `logitfdepot` (F) | logit(0.74) | Table III (F = 74%); Eq. 1 logit parameterization |
| `lksyn` (ksyn) | 51.9 ng/mL/day | Table III |
| `lkdeg` (kdeg) | 0.22 1/day | Table III |
| `lkss` (Kss) | 18.8 ng/mL | Table III |
| `lkint` (kint) | 0.0345 1/day | Table III |
| `e_wt_cl`, `e_wt_vc` | 0.75, 1 (fixed) | Table III footnote a; Results |
| `etalcl`, `etalka`, `etalkint` block | CV 25.1, 59.5, 42.3%; cov -0.0731, 0.0682 | Table III |
| `etalvc` | CV 43.8% | Table III |
| `expSd` | 0.179 | Table III; Supplementary Methods (ln-transformed fit) |
| `lrbase_cidbf` (dDBF0) | 398 PU | Table IV |
| `lic50` (IC50) | 255 ng/mL | Table IV |
| `limax` (Imax) | 0.893 | Table IV |
| `lhill` (Hill) | 3.08 | Table IV |
| `etalrbase_cidbf`, `etalic50` | CV 28.3%, 94.1% | Table IV |
| `addSd_cidbf`, `propSd_cidbf` | 23.8 PU, 21.9% | Table IV; Supplementary Methods |
| `etaRUV_cidbf` | CV 38.7% | Table IV ('Residual error' row with eta shrinkage) |
| `d/dt(depot)`, `f(depot)` | -- | Eq. 1 |
| Unbound concentration (QSS root) | -- | Eq. 2 |
| `d/dt(total_target)`, `total_target(0) = ksyn/kdeg` | -- | text under Eq. 2 |
| `d/dt(central)` (total drug) | -- | Eq. 3 |
| `d/dt(peripheral1)` (unbound drug) | -- | Eq. 4 |
| `cidbf` | -- | Eq. 7 |

BSV is printed as %CV, which the table footnote calls an approximation of the
coefficient of variation; the variances are `CV^2`. That reading is confirmed by
the printed covariances, which reproduce the correlations quoted in the Results
only under it (checked below).

# Parameter identities

The paper prints several quantities derived from the estimates. They are
deterministic functions of `ini()`, so they are checked exactly (to the
precision printed).

```{r identities}
mod <- readModelDb("Vu_2017_erenumab")
ui <- rxode2::rxode2(mod)
th <- ui$theta
p <- exp(th[c("lcl", "lvc", "lka", "lksyn", "lkdeg", "lkss", "lkint", "lic50", "lhill")])
names(p) <- sub("^l", "", names(p))
om <- ui$omega

ident <- tibble::tribble(
  ~quantity, ~model, ~paper,
  "Absorption half-life (day)", log(2) / p[["ka"]], 1.6,
  "CL/Vc (1/day)", p[["cl"]] / p[["vc"]], 0.0501,
  "Rtot,ss = ksyn/kdeg (ng/mL)", p[["ksyn"]] / p[["kdeg"]], NA,
  "Max. nonlinear CL = kint*Vc*Rtot,ss/Kss (L/day)",
  p[["kint"]] * p[["vc"]] * (p[["ksyn"]] / p[["kdeg"]]) / p[["kss"]], 1.84,
  "IC99 = 99^(1/hill) * IC50 (ng/mL)", 99^(1 / p[["hill"]]) * p[["ic50"]], 1134,
  "corr(eta CL, eta ka)", om["etalcl", "etalka"] / sqrt(om["etalcl", "etalcl"] * om["etalka", "etalka"]), -0.49,
  "corr(eta CL, eta kint)", om["etalcl", "etalkint"] / sqrt(om["etalcl", "etalcl"] * om["etalkint", "etalkint"]), 0.642
)
knitr::kable(ident, digits = 4)

chk <- ident |> filter(!is.na(paper))
stopifnot(all(abs(chk$model / chk$paper - 1) < 0.02))
```

The Results quote maximal nonlinear clearance as "approximately 1.84 L/day"
(1.85 here) and about 8 times the linear clearance (1.85 / 0.214 = 8.6).

# Drug-free baseline

The receptor pool starts at `ksyn/kdeg` and the CIDBF response at its baseline,
so an undosed (placebo) solve must stay flat. Both sides share the same
parameters, so a tight bound is correct.

```{r baseline}
mod_typ <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod)

# Two endpoints (Cc and cidbf): every observation row carries dvid = 1 so it
# maps to an endpoint; both observables are returned as columns regardless.
obs_rows <- function(times, id = 1L) {
  data.frame(id = id, time = times, amt = NA_real_, evid = 0L,
             cmt = NA_character_, dvid = 1L)
}
dose_rows <- function(times, amt, cmt, id = 1L) {
  data.frame(id = id, time = times, amt = amt, evid = 1L,
             cmt = cmt, dvid = NA_integer_)
}
build <- function(dose, obs, wt = 70) {
  ev <- dplyr::bind_rows(dose, obs)
  ev$WT <- wt
  ev[order(ev$id, ev$time, -ev$evid), ]
}

pl <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typ, build(NULL, obs_rows(seq(0, 200, by = 5))),
                      returnType = "data.frame")
c(max_rtot_drift = max(abs(pl$total_target - p[["ksyn"]] / p[["kdeg"]])),
  max_cidbf_drift = max(abs(pl$cidbf - 398)))
stopifnot(max(abs(pl$total_target - p[["ksyn"]] / p[["kdeg"]])) < 1e-6,
          max(abs(pl$cidbf - 398)) < 1e-6)
```

# Typical-value profiles against Figure 2

```{r typical}
grid <- sort(unique(c(0, 0.02, 0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 10,
                      seq(12, 56, by = 2), seq(63, 224, by = 7))))
regimens <- tibble::tribble(
  ~regimen, ~amt, ~cmt, ~times,
  "1 mg SC", 1, "depot", list(0),
  "7 mg SC", 7, "depot", list(0),
  "21 mg SC", 21, "depot", list(0),
  "70 mg SC", 70, "depot", list(0),
  "140 mg SC", 140, "depot", list(0),
  "140 mg IV", 140, "central", list(0),
  "210 mg SC", 210, "depot", list(0),
  "21 mg SC Q4W", 21, "depot", list(c(0, 28, 56)),
  "70 mg SC Q4W", 70, "depot", list(c(0, 28, 56)),
  "140 mg SC Q4W", 140, "depot", list(c(0, 28, 56))
)
typ <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(regimens)), function(i) {
  r <- regimens[i, ]
  s <- rxode2::rxSolve(
    mod_typ,
    build(dose_rows(unlist(r$times), r$amt, r$cmt), obs_rows(grid)),
    returnType = "data.frame"
  )
  s$regimen <- r$regimen
  s
}) |> dplyr::bind_rows()
typ$regimen <- factor(typ$regimen, levels = regimens$regimen)

typ_peak <- typ |>
  filter(time <= 28) |>
  group_by(regimen) |>
  summarise(Cmax_first = max(Cc), tmax_first = time[which.max(Cc)],
            Cc_day28 = Cc[time == 28], .groups = "drop")
knitr::kable(typ_peak, digits = c(0, 0, 1, 0),
             caption = "Typical-value (70 kg) unbound erenumab, first dosing interval.")
```

The Figure 2 VPC medians peak at roughly 300 ng/mL for 7 mg SC, roughly
5000 ng/mL for 70 mg SC and start near 30000 ng/mL after 140 mg IV (read off
the log-scale panels by the maintainers). The typical-value solve reproduces
these within the reading precision of the figure.

```{r fig2-gate}
fig2 <- c("7 mg SC" = 300, "70 mg SC" = 5000)
got <- setNames(typ_peak$Cmax_first, typ_peak$regimen)[names(fig2)]
iv0 <- typ$Cc[typ$regimen == "140 mg IV" & typ$time == 0.02]
rbind(model = c(got, "140 mg IV (t = 0+)" = iv0),
      figure2 = c(fig2, 30000))
stopifnot(all(abs(got / fig2 - 1) < 0.35), abs(iv0 / 30000 - 1) < 0.35)
```

Target-mediated elimination makes exposure more than dose proportional at low
doses; at high doses the receptor sink is saturated and the dose-normalized
exposure approaches the linear limit `F / CL`.

```{r nonlinearity}
dn <- typ |>
  filter(regimen %in% c("1 mg SC", "7 mg SC", "21 mg SC", "70 mg SC",
                        "140 mg SC", "210 mg SC")) |>
  group_by(regimen) |>
  summarise(auc = sum(diff(time) * (head(Cc, -1) + tail(Cc, -1)) / 2),
            .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(dose = as.numeric(sub(" mg SC", "", regimen)),
         # AUC in ng*day/mL; F*Dose/CL in mg*day/L = ug*day/mL, x 1000
         auc_over_linear_limit = auc / (1000 * 0.74 * dose / p[["cl"]]))
knitr::kable(dn, digits = 3)
stopifnot(all(diff(dn$auc_over_linear_limit) > 0),
          dn$auc_over_linear_limit[dn$dose == 210] > 0.8,
          dn$auc_over_linear_limit[dn$dose == 1] < 0.3)
```

# Virtual cohort

Observed data are not public. Each arm below is a virtual cohort of 100
subjects with body weight drawn from a normal distribution matching Table II
(mean 74.9 kg, SD 11.9 kg), rejected and redrawn outside the observed
49-104 kg range.

```{r cohort}
set.seed(20170917)
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20170917)
n_per_arm <- 100

draw_wt <- function(n) {
  wt <- rnorm(n, 74.9, 11.9)
  bad <- wt < 49 | wt > 104
  while (any(bad)) {
    wt[bad] <- rnorm(sum(bad), 74.9, 11.9)
    bad <- wt < 49 | wt > 104
  }
  wt
}

make_cohort <- function(n, regimen, dose_times, amt, cmt, obs, id_offset) {
  ids <- id_offset + seq_len(n)
  wt <- draw_wt(n)
  ev <- lapply(seq_len(n), function(j) {
    d <- if (amt > 0) {
      data.frame(id = ids[j], time = dose_times,
                 amt = amt,
                 evid = 1L, cmt = cmt, dvid = NA_integer_)
    } else {
      NULL
    }
    e <- dplyr::bind_rows(d, data.frame(id = ids[j], time = obs, amt = NA_real_,
                                        evid = 0L, cmt = NA_character_, dvid = 1L))
    e$WT <- wt[j]
    e
  }) |> dplyr::bind_rows()
  ev$regimen <- regimen
  ev
}

arms <- tibble::tribble(
  ~regimen, ~amt, ~cmt, ~times,
  "Placebo", 0, "depot", list(0),
  "1 mg SC", 1, "depot", list(0),
  "7 mg SC", 7, "depot", list(0),
  "21 mg SC", 21, "depot", list(0),
  "70 mg SC", 70, "depot", list(0),
  "140 mg SC", 140, "depot", list(0),
  "140 mg IV", 140, "central", list(0),
  "210 mg SC", 210, "depot", list(0),
  "21 mg SC Q4W", 21, "depot", list(c(0, 28, 56)),
  "70 mg SC Q4W", 70, "depot", list(c(0, 28, 56)),
  "140 mg SC Q4W", 140, "depot", list(c(0, 28, 56))
)
events <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(arms)), function(i) {
  make_cohort(n_per_arm, arms$regimen[i], unlist(arms$times[[i]]), arms$amt[i],
              arms$cmt[i], grid, id_offset = (i - 1L) * n_per_arm)
}) |> dplyr::bind_rows()
events <- events[order(events$id, events$time, -events$evid), ]
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(unique(events[, c("id", "time", "evid")])))

# 280 mg then 210 mg x 2 Q4W
extra <- make_cohort(n_per_arm, "280/210 mg SC Q4W", c(0, 28, 56), 210, "depot",
                     grid, id_offset = nrow(arms) * n_per_arm)
extra$amt[extra$evid == 1L & extra$time == 0] <- 280
events <- dplyr::bind_rows(events, extra)
events <- events[order(events$id, events$time, -events$evid), ]
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(unique(events[, c("id", "time", "evid")])))
```

# Simulation

```{r simulate}
sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = events, keep = c("regimen", "WT"),
                       returnType = "data.frame")
sim$regimen <- factor(sim$regimen, levels = c(arms$regimen, "280/210 mg SC Q4W"))
```

# Replicate published figures

## Figure 2 -- PK VPC

```{r figure-2, fig.height = 6}
# Replicates Figure 2 of Vu 2017: model-predicted median and 90% interval of
# serum (unbound) erenumab concentration by cohort.
sim |>
  filter(regimen != "Placebo", time >= 0.1) |>
  group_by(regimen, time) |>
  summarise(Q05 = quantile(Cc, 0.05), Q50 = median(Cc), Q95 = quantile(Cc, 0.95),
            .groups = "drop") |>
  ggplot(aes(time / 7, Q50)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = pmax(Q05, 1), ymax = Q95), fill = "orange", alpha = 0.2) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~regimen, scales = "free") +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "Time after dose (weeks)", y = "Serum erenumab (ng/mL)",
       caption = "Replicates Figure 2 of Vu 2017 (simulated, no observed data).")
```

## Figure 3 -- CIDBF VPC

```{r figure-3, fig.height = 6}
# Replicates Figure 3 of Vu 2017: capsaicin-induced dermal blood flow response.
sim |>
  group_by(regimen, time) |>
  summarise(Q05 = quantile(cidbf, 0.05), Q50 = median(cidbf),
            Q95 = quantile(cidbf, 0.95), .groups = "drop") |>
  ggplot(aes(time / 7, Q50)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = Q05, ymax = Q95), fill = "orange", alpha = 0.2) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~regimen) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, 32)) +
  labs(x = "Time after first dose (weeks)", y = "Dermal blood flow response (PU)",
       caption = "Replicates Figure 3 of Vu 2017 (individual predictions, no residual error).")
```

The Figure 3 medians sit at about 400 PU on placebo and fall to about 40 PU
(`398 * (1 - 0.893) = 42.6`) while concentrations stay above IC99. The
placebo median is a centre statistic of the baseline distribution, so it is
checked against 398 PU with a tolerance; the typical-value nadir is exact.

```{r figure-3-gate}
plc_med <- median(sim$cidbf[sim$regimen == "Placebo"])
nadir_typ <- min(typ$cidbf[typ$regimen == "140 mg SC"])
c(placebo_median = plc_med, typical_nadir_140mg = nadir_typ)
stopifnot(abs(plc_med / 398 - 1) < 0.1,
          abs(nadir_typ - 398 * (1 - 0.893)) < 1)
```

## Figure 4 -- concentration-inhibition relationship

```{r figure-4}
# Replicates the typical profile of Figure 4 of Vu 2017.
conc <- 10^seq(-1, 5, length.out = 300)
inh_curve <- data.frame(
  conc = conc,
  inh = 100 * 0.893 * conc^3.08 / (255^3.08 + conc^3.08)
)
ggplot(inh_curve, aes(conc, inh)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.99 * 89.3, linetype = 2, colour = "red") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 1134, linetype = 2, colour = "red") +
  scale_x_log10() +
  labs(x = "Erenumab concentration (ng/mL)", y = "DBF inhibition (%)",
       caption = "Replicates Figure 4 of Vu 2017 (typical profile).")

# The model's own inhibition at IC99 is 99% of Imax by construction.
s99 <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  mod_typ,
  build(dose_rows(0, 1000, "central"), obs_rows(c(0.001, 1, 5, 10, 20, 40, 60))),
  returnType = "data.frame"
)
k <- which.min(abs(s99$Cc - 1134))
stopifnot(abs(s99$inh[k] / 0.893 -
                s99$Cc[k]^3.08 / (255^3.08 + s99$Cc[k]^3.08)) < 1e-8)
```

## Figure 5 -- phase 2 dose-selection simulation

Figure 5 simulated 7, 21 and 70 mg SC monthly for 12 weeks followed by
open-label 70 mg monthly to week 48 (100 subjects per cohort, Supplementary
Methods), and showed the median and 90% interval of concentration and of DBF
inhibition as a percentage of Imax.

```{r figure-5}
p2_obs <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 448, by = 2), seq(450, 448 + 140, by = 7))))
p2 <- lapply(seq_along(c(7, 21, 70)), function(i) {
  d <- c(7, 21, 70)[i]
  ev <- make_cohort(n_per_arm, paste(d, "mg"), seq(0, 336, by = 28), d,
                    "depot", p2_obs, id_offset = 10000L + (i - 1L) * n_per_arm)
  ev$amt[ev$evid == 1L & ev$time >= 84] <- 70
  ev
}) |> dplyr::bind_rows()
p2 <- p2[order(p2$id, p2$time, -p2$evid), ]
sim5 <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = p2, keep = "regimen", returnType = "data.frame") |>
  mutate(pct_imax = 100 * inh / 0.893)

sum5 <- sim5 |>
  group_by(regimen, time) |>
  summarise(across(c(Cc, pct_imax),
                   list(q05 = ~ quantile(.x, 0.05), q50 = median, q95 = ~ quantile(.x, 0.95))),
            .groups = "drop")

ggplot(filter(sum5, time > 0), aes(time / 7, Cc_q50, colour = regimen)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_line(aes(y = pmax(Cc_q05, 1)), linetype = 2) +
  geom_line(aes(y = Cc_q95), linetype = 2) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = c(255, 1134)) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "Weeks", y = "Erenumab (ng/mL)",
       caption = "Replicates Figure 5 (left) of Vu 2017.")

ggplot(sum5, aes(time / 7, pct_imax_q50, colour = regimen)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_line(aes(y = pct_imax_q05), linetype = 2) +
  geom_line(aes(y = pct_imax_q95), linetype = 2) +
  labs(x = "Weeks", y = "DBF inhibition (% of Imax)",
       caption = "Replicates Figure 5 (right) of Vu 2017 (no residual error).")
```

The Results state that 21 mg Q4W places more than half of the subjects above
IC99 after the second dose, and that 70 mg Q4W holds full inhibition through
the dosing interval.

```{r figure-5-gate}
dose2_peak <- sim5 |>
  filter(regimen == "21 mg", time > 28, time <= 56) |>
  group_by(id) |>
  summarise(cmax = max(Cc), .groups = "drop")
trough70 <- sim5 |>
  filter(regimen == "70 mg", time == 84) |>
  pull(pct_imax)
c(frac_21mg_above_ic99_dose2 = mean(dose2_peak$cmax > 1134),
  median_pct_imax_70mg_trough3 = median(trough70))
stopifnot(median(dose2_peak$cmax) > 1134, median(trough70) > 95)
```

# PKNCA validation

The paper reports no NCA, so PKNCA is used to summarize the simulated
single-dose cohorts (unbound erenumab) without a published comparator.

```{r pknca}
sad <- c("1 mg SC", "7 mg SC", "21 mg SC", "70 mg SC", "140 mg SC",
         "140 mg IV", "210 mg SC")
sim_nca <- sim |>
  filter(regimen %in% sad, !is.na(Cc)) |>
  mutate(treatment = as.character(regimen)) |>
  select(id, time, Cc, treatment)
sim_nca <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  sim_nca,
  sim_nca |> distinct(id, treatment) |> mutate(time = 0, Cc = 0)
) |>
  distinct(id, treatment, time, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  arrange(id, treatment, time)
# IV bolus: the time-zero value is the first post-dose concentration, not 0.
iv_first <- sim_nca |> filter(treatment == "140 mg IV", time > 0) |>
  group_by(id) |> slice(1) |> ungroup()
sim_nca <- sim_nca |>
  left_join(iv_first |> select(id, c0 = Cc), by = "id") |>
  mutate(Cc = ifelse(treatment == "140 mg IV" & time == 0, c0, Cc)) |>
  select(-c0)

dose_df <- events |>
  filter(evid == 1, regimen %in% sad) |>
  mutate(treatment = regimen) |>
  select(id, time, amt, treatment)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(sim_nca, Cc ~ time | treatment + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | treatment + id)
intervals <- data.frame(start = 0, end = Inf, cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE,
                        aucinf.obs = TRUE, half.life = TRUE)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))
nca_sum <- as.data.frame(nca_res$result) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "tmax", "aucinf.obs", "half.life")) |>
  group_by(treatment, PPTESTCD) |>
  summarise(median = median(PPORRES, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = median) |>
  mutate(treatment = factor(treatment, levels = sad)) |>
  arrange(treatment)
nca_sum |>
  rename("Cohort" = treatment, "Cmax (ng/mL)" = cmax, "Tmax (day)" = tmax,
         "AUCinf (ng*day/mL)" = aucinf.obs, "t1/2 (day)" = half.life) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = "Median simulated NCA of unbound erenumab.")
```

The median Tmax of the SC cohorts (about 4-6 days) is consistent with the
paper's absorption half-life of 1.6 days and its statement that SC absorption
is essentially complete within about 8 days.

```{r pknca-gate}
sc_tmax <- nca_sum$tmax[nca_sum$treatment %in% c("70 mg SC", "140 mg SC", "210 mg SC")]
stopifnot(all(sc_tmax > 2 & sc_tmax < 10))
```

# Assumptions and deviations

- **Observed concentration.** The paper estimated Kss "directly from the
  available unbound serum erenumab concentration data", so `Cc` is the unbound
  concentration of Eq. 2, and the PD model (Eq. 7, "[AMG334]") is driven by the
  same quantity.
- **Amount and concentration units.** Doses are in mg and volumes in L, while
  Rtot, Kss, ksyn and IC50 are in ng/mL; the model converts the central amount
  to ng/mL with a factor of 1000. The receptor pool is carried in
  erenumab-mass-equivalent concentration, as the paper does.
- **Bioavailability parameterization.** Eq. 1 estimates F on a logit scale
  (`1/(1 + exp(F))`); only the back-transformed 74% is printed, so the model
  carries `logit(0.74)` with no between-subject variability.
- **BSV scale.** BSV is printed as %CV, and variances are taken as `CV^2`; this
  reproduces both correlations quoted in the Results (-0.49 and 0.642), which
  the log-normal `log(1 + CV^2)` form does not (-0.54).
- **ka-kint covariance.** Only the CL-ka and CL-kint covariances are printed,
  so the ka-kint covariance is 0.
- **IIV on the DBF residual error.** Table IV lists a second "Residual error"
  row (38.7% CV, 33.3% shrinkage) beside the BSV rows; it is read as
  between-subject variability on the residual-error magnitude (NONMEM
  `W * EXP(ETA)`), applied to both the additive and proportional components.
  It is named `etaRUV_cidbf` after the existing `etaRUV` / `etaRUV_<output>`
  models; because it scales two residual parameters at once there is no single
  fixed effect for it to pair with, which `checkModelConventions()` reports as
  a naming warning.
- **Combined residual error form.** The Supplementary Methods describe the DBF
  error as `Y = Ypred + W * eps` with W additive, proportional "or a
  combination" without giving the combination formula; nlmixr2's default
  `add() + prop()` (variances summed) is used.
- **IV administration.** The 140 mg IV dose is entered as a bolus into
  `central` (Eq. 3 initial condition `Atot(0) = DoseIV`); the infusion
  duration is not reported.
- **Figure 5 low-dose cohorts.** The typical-value peaks agree with the
  Figure 2 VPC medians for the 7 mg SC, 70 mg SC and 140 mg IV panels (gated
  above), and the 70 mg simulation agrees with the Figure 5 projection. For
  7 and 21 mg, the Figure 5 medians peak lower than simulated here (about 150
  versus 300 ng/mL for 7 mg and 1000 versus 1360 ng/mL for 21 mg after the
  first dose, read off the figure by the maintainers). The covariate set sampled for Figure 5 is not printed, and
  Figure 2 is the fitted-model VPC, so the packaged parameters are used as
  printed and the low-dose difference is not gated.
- **Covariates screened but not retained.** Sex, age and population type
  (healthy versus migraine) were tested and not retained; they are recorded in
  `covariatesDataExcluded`.
- **Errata.** No correction notice for this article was found on PubMed or
  Europe PMC (checked 2026-11-25).
